source.title: Official Docker image 2.43.3 ships @napi-rs/canvas without any native binding → "DOMMatrix is not defined" in all PDF nodes

source.body:
### Bug Description

PDF parsing fails in the official Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.43.3` with
`DOMMatrix is not defined`. Both independent PDF code paths are affected:

- `n8n-nodes-base.extractFromFile` (operation: `pdf`)
- `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.documentDefaultDataLoader` (dataType: `binary`, loader: `pdfLoader`)

Downloading the PDF (e.g. via HTTP Request node) works fine; the failure
happens only when the PDF is parsed.

**Root cause:** the image contains the JS wrapper `@napi-rs/canvas@0.1.80`,
but **no platform-specific native binding at all**. Neither
`@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl` (which this Alpine/musl x86_64 image would
need) nor any other variant is present. As a result, pdfjs-dist cannot
polyfill `DOMMatrix`, `ImageData` and `Path2D`, and PDF parsing aborts.

This is reproducible in a **pristine** image with no mounts, environment
variables or customizations.

### To Reproduce

1. Check which `@napi-rs/canvas` packages ship with the image:

```bash
   docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3 -c \
     'ls /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm | grep -i "napi-rs+canvas"'
```

   Output:

```
   @napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80
```

   Only the wrapper is present; no `canvas-linux-x64-musl` (nor `-gnu`).

2. Try to load the package inside the pristine image:

```bash
   docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3 -c \
     'd=$(find / -type d -path "*node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas" 2>/dev/null | head -1); \
      echo "Path: $d"; node -e "require(\"$d\"); console.log(\"canvas OK\")"'
```

   Output:

```
   Path: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80/node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas
   Error: Failed to load native binding
     [cause]: [
       Error: Cannot find module './skia.linux-x64-musl.node'
       Error: Cannot find module '@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl'
     ]
```

3. In a running instance, execute any workflow that uses Extract from File
   (operation: PDF) or the Default Data Loader with a PDF binary. The node
   fails with `DOMMatrix is not defined`.

### Expected behavior

The image ships the native `@napi-rs/canvas` binding matching its own
platform (`linux-x64-musl`, and `linux-arm64-musl` for arm64 images), so
PDF extraction works out of the box.

### Debug Info

## Logs (running instance)

```
Warning: Cannot load "@napi-rs/canvas" package: "Error: Failed to load native binding".
Warning: Cannot polyfill `DOMMatrix`, rendering may be broken.
Warning: Cannot polyfill `ImageData`, rendering may be broken.
Warning: Cannot polyfill `Path2D`, rendering may be broken.
ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined
```

## Environment

- n8n version: 2.43.3 (self-hosted, `N8N_RELEASE_TYPE=stable`)
- Image: `docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3`
  (digest `sha256:d4eca183959b30fb1ba5ecda7e58363c5be49a7bcf8c0227a6384a47ce2f7a65`)
- Base OS (from image): Docker Hardened Images (Alpine) 3.24
- Node.js: v26.7.0
- Architecture: x86_64
- Running via: Docker, with external task runners
  (`n8nio/runners:2.43.3`, `N8N_RUNNERS_MODE=external`)
- Database / binary data mode: not relevant (reproducible without any instance data)

## Additional context

- Earlier images did contain `skia.linux-x64-musl.node` (see #23754 for 2.0.0),
  so this appears to be a packaging regression: the optional platform
  dependencies of `@napi-rs/canvas` seem to be omitted entirely during the
  image build (e.g. via `--no-optional`, production pruning, or pnpm not
  resolving optional deps for the target platform).
- Related historical reports of the same symptom: #16593, #16438, #16422.
- Possible fix: make sure the Docker build installs the matching platform
  package, e.g. by adding `@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl` /
  `@napi-rs/canvas-linux-arm64-musl` explicitly, or by configuring pnpm
  `supportedArchitectures` with `os: ["linux"]`, `cpu: ["x64", "arm64"]`,
  `libc: ["musl"]`.
- Current workaround: extract the PDF text outside of n8n (e.g. Python/pypdf)
  and send the text to n8n via webhook.

### Operating System

Debian 13 (host); container: Alpine 3.24 (Docker Hardened Images, official n8nio/n8n image)

### n8n Version

2.43.3

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: WilliamAyad
comments.text:
+1 — reproduced identically on a pristine pull of docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3.
The wrapper @napi-rs/canvas@0.1.80 is present but no platform binding ships with
it (this Alpine-based image needs @napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl), so pdfjs-dist
cannot polyfill DOMMatrix/ImageData/Path2D and every PDF code path dies.

Immediate unblock, pick one:

1) Easiest: pin back to docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.2 until a fixed image is published.

2) If you must stay on 2.43.3, bake the matching binding into the image:

FROM docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3
USER root
RUN cd /tmp && npm pack @napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl@0.1.80 \
 && tar -xzf napi-rs-canvas-linux-x64-musl-0.1.80.tgz \
 && cp package/canvas.linux-x64-musl.node \
     /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80/node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas/ \
 && rm -rf /tmp/package /tmp/*.tgz
USER node

The binding version must match the wrapper (0.1.80). On ARM hosts use
@napi-rs/canvas-linux-arm64-musl; on a Debian/glibc base it would be the -gnu
variant. (Confirm the wrapper's exact .pnpm path with the `ls ... grep napi-rs+canvas`
command from the original report, in case it shifts between tags.)

3) Cheap CI smoke gate so a regression like this never reaches your prod again:

docker run --rm --entrypoint node your-n8n-image -e \
  "require('/usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80/node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas')"

(exit 0 = binding loads; fail the deploy otherwise.)

Root-cause suspicion for the maintainers: the image build now appears to prune
npm optional dependencies. napi-rs ships its platform binaries as
optionalDependencies of the wrapper, so an --omit=optional-style publish step
strips exactly the .node file pdfjs needs — worth checking the publish pipeline
for that flag.

comments.author: nephilim75
comments.text:
Additional data points — the issue is not limited to 2.43.3:

| Version | `@napi-rs/canvas` binding loads? |
|---|---|
| 2.43.2 | ❌ `Failed to load native binding` (only `@napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80` present) |
| 2.43.3 | ❌ same |
| 2.44.3 | ❌ same (Node.js v26.10.0) |

So pinning back to 2.43.2, as suggested above, does **not** work around it.

Thanks @mayanksingh-27 for #41312 — happy to test a built image once available.
